# PV-MEPCG / PulseVision -- configuration reference

Generated by `python scripts/48_project_docs.py` -- do not edit by hand.

Every key in every file under `configs/`, with the default as **declared in the
YAML** -- not as resolved at runtime. `paths.yaml` values are shown relative,
because `src/utils/config.py` resolves them against the repository root at load
time and printing this machine's absolute paths into a committed document would
be wrong on every other machine.

## How a value is read, and how to override one

```python
from src.utils.config import load_config
cfg = load_config('signal')
cfg['filter.low_hz']            # dotted access; a missing level names the full path
cfg.get('filter.low_hz', 20)    # with a default
```

Any leaf can be overridden without editing a file, using
`HEARTGUARD__<FILE>__<KEY__PATH>` (double underscores between levels):

```powershell
$env:HEARTGUARD__SIGNAL__RESAMPLE__TARGET_FS = "4000"   # PowerShell
```

```bash
export HEARTGUARD__MODELS__GLOBAL__N_JOBS=4              # bash
```

Values are parsed as YAML scalars, so `4000` arrives as an `int` and `true` as a
`bool`. **Every override that fires is recorded in the run manifest** -- an
override that changes a result and leaves no trace would break research rule 5.

Four things are validated at load and are errors, not warnings: the feature
counts must still sum to 138, the filter passband must stay below Nyquist at the
target sampling rate, band-power edges must stay inside the passband, and an
unknown top-level key is rejected rather than silently ignored.

> **Write scientific notation with a signed exponent.** PyYAML is YAML 1.1:
> `1.0e3` parses as the *string* `"1.0e3"`, `1.0e+3` as a float.

## Contents

- [`configs/experiments.yaml`](#configsexperimentsyaml) -- experiment declarations, cross-validation, search budgets and selection rules
- [`configs/features.yaml`](#configsfeaturesyaml) -- the 138-feature registry's parameters, per family
- [`configs/models.yaml`](#configsmodelsyaml) -- the eight models, their search spaces, calibration and class weighting
- [`configs/paths.yaml`](#configspathsyaml) -- every path in the project, resolved against the repository root
- [`configs/signal.yaml`](#configssignalyaml) -- resampling, filtering, normalization, segmentation and signal quality

## `configs/signal.yaml`

Resampling, filtering, normalization, segmentation and signal quality.

| Key | Default | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resample` |  | section | --- resampling (Phase 23) -------------------------------------------------- |
| `resample.target_fs` | `2000` | int | Hz. All four datasets are brought to this rate. |
| `resample.method` | `soxr_hq` | str | high-quality anti-aliased polyphase resampler |
| `resample.native_fs` |  | section | PASCAL A is 44100 Hz -> 2000 Hz, a factor of 22.05. Naive decimation (x[::22]) aliases badly at this ratio; T23.4 verifies with a swept sine. |
| `resample.native_fs.d1_physionet` | `2000` | int | no-op path |
| `resample.native_fs.d2_pascal_a` | `44100` | int | 22.05x decimation |
| `resample.native_fs.d3_pascal_b` | `4000` | int | 2x decimation |
| `resample.native_fs.d4_circor` | `4000` | int | 2x decimation |
| `resample.mono` | `mean` | str | channel mean; no-op fast path (all files mono) |
| `resample.dtype` | `float32` | str |  |
| `filter` |  | section | --- bandpass filter (Phase 24) --------------------------------------------- |
| `filter.enabled` | `true` | bool | ablation PP-09 flips this |
| `filter.type` | `butterworth` | str |  |
| `filter.order` | `4` | int | prototype order. The bandpass transform doubles it |
| `filter.low_hz` | `20` | int |  |
| `filter.high_hz` | `400` | int | well below the 1000 Hz Nyquist at target_fs |
| `filter.design` | `sos` | str | second-order sections; numerically stable at order 4 |
| `filter.zero_phase` | `true` | bool | scipy.signal.sosfiltfilt |
| `filter.short_signal_policy` | `reduce_padlen` | str | 0.76 s, is 1,520 samples at 2 kHz. An earlier draft of this comment claimed the opposite; Phase 24 measured it. The guard below reduces padding and flags the record rather than raising, and exists for the inference API, where an uploaded clip can be any length. |
| `filter.min_padlen` | `12` | int |  |
| `normalization` |  | section | --- normalization (Phase 25) ----------------------------------------------- |
| `normalization.enabled` | `true` | bool | ablation PP-09 flips this |
| `normalization.method` | `zscore` | str | alternatives: "peak", "none" |
| `normalization.remove_dc` | `true` | bool | subtract the mean before normalizing |
| `normalization.zero_variance_epsilon` | `1e-10` | float | Guard against a constant / all-silent record producing division by zero. |
| `normalization.zero_variance_policy` | `passthrough_and_flag` | str |  |
| `quality` |  | section | --- signal quality analysis (Phase 26) ------------------------------------- |
| `quality.clipping_threshold` | `0.99` | float | \|sample\| above this counts as clipped |
| `quality.clipping_ratio_flag` | `0.01` | float | >1% clipped samples -> flagged |
| `quality.silence_threshold_db` | `-60.0` | float | frame RMS below this counts as silence |
| `quality.silence_ratio_flag` | `0.5` | float |  |
| `quality.snr_proxy` |  | section |  |
| `quality.snr_proxy.in_band` | `[20, 400]` | list | must match filter.low_hz / filter.high_hz |
| `quality.snr_proxy.out_of_band` | `[400, 1000]` | list | up to Nyquist at target_fs |
| `quality.snr_proxy.low_snr_db_flag` | `5.0` | float |  |
| `quality.spectral_flatness_flag` | `0.5` | float | above this the record is noise-like |
| `quality.drift_ratio_db_flag` | `5.0` | float | +5.0 dB was chosen from the sweep in outputs/02_preprocessing/ sqi_calibration.csv, not by eye. The two proxies above are KEPT: they fire on out-of-band and white-noise-like records that this one misses, mostly in CirCor. See the 2026-08-26 Phases 26-27 entry in Docs/note.md. |
| `quality.short_duration_sec` | `2.0` | float | is_short threshold |
| `quality.calibrate_against_sqi` | `true` | bool | Thresholds are calibrated against PhysioNet REFERENCE-SQI as an independent human-annotated reference (T26.5) rather than chosen by eye. |
| `framing` |  | section | --- framing (shared by quality analysis and the frequency/MFCC families) ---- |
| `framing.frame_length` | `512` | int | 256 ms at 2000 Hz |
| `framing.hop_length` | `256` | int | 128 ms, 50% overlap |
| `framing.window` | `hann` | str |  |
| `framing.center` | `true` | bool |  |
| `cache` |  | section | --- preprocessing cache (Phase 27) ----------------------------------------- |
| `cache.enabled` | `true` | bool |  |
| `cache.format` | `npy` | str |  |
| `cache.hash_config` | `true` | bool | cache key = record_uid + hash of this file |
| `integrity` |  | section | T27.3 note: when the preprocessed-signal cache key is built, hash the resample / filter / normalization / framing sections only. Hashing this whole file would make a change to an audit threshold invalidate every cached preprocessed signal, which is unrelated work. |
| `integrity.silence_peak` | `0.001` | float | signal. One definition of silence for the whole project, not two. An earlier draft used 1e-4 (-80 dBFS), chosen by eye, and it missed the one genuinely dead recording in the corpus: set_a's Aunlabelledtest__201106120928 peaks at -71 dBFS over its full 9 seconds. |
| `integrity.constant_variance` | `1e-12` | float |  |
| `integrity.clipping_threshold` | `0.99` | float | T16.4 -- full-scale samples. Shares its definition with quality.clipping_* above, which applies the same test to the preprocessed signal in Phase 26. |
| `integrity.clipping_ratio_flag` | `0.01` | float |  |
| `integrity.min_samples` | `2` | int | T16.2 -- a file shorter than this holds too few samples to be a recording at any of the three native rates; treated as truncated rather than short. |
| `integrity.content_hash_fs` | `2000` | int | T17.2 -- the canonical form an audio-content hash is computed on: mono, resampled to this rate, quantized to this many decimal places. Quantizing matters because two resamplers, or two library versions, will not agree in the last float bits on an otherwise identical signal. |
| `integrity.content_hash_decimals` | `5` | int |  |
| `integrity.envelope_points` | `256` | int | T17.4 -- near-duplicate detection. Envelopes are resampled to a fixed length so recordings of different durations remain comparable, then correlated within each dataset. |
| `integrity.near_duplicate_correlation` | `0.98` | float |  |
| `integrity.duration_bands` |  | section | T18.3 -- robustness duration bands, in seconds. |
| `integrity.duration_bands.short_below` | `5.0` | float |  |
| `integrity.duration_bands.long_above` | `20.0` | float |  |
